node.body:
Thanks for pointing out the second-order case. I ran the same uniform transient MMS with `DUAL_TIME_STEPPING-2ND_ORDER` on the pinned v8.5.0 runtime (`12eb826f049ef7f67df974dfcb44cf36ee07c0f8`). The original driver does show first-order source-lag error in this control.

For `u_x=1+t^2`, `f_x=2t`, final time 0.5:

| dt | Original endpoint max error | Existing time-shift intervention |
|---|---:|---:|
| 0.1 | 0.08506172841 | 0.004979423888 |
| 0.05 | 0.04625006353 | 0.001249978856 |
| 0.025 | 0.02406250002 | 0.0003125000269 |

Observed orders: 0.87905, 0.94267 versus 1.99408, 1.99998. Every saved step satisfies all four log10 residual thresholds below -10, and spatial spreads remain below 5.30e-11.

Including the repeated startup history `U[-1]=U[0]=1`, the old-time recurrence is
`3U[k]-4U[k-1]+U[k-2]=4h^2(k-1)`, with exact error
`e[k]=-2*k*h^2+(3/2)*h^2*(1-3^(-k))`.
At fixed `T=k*h`, this is `-2*T*h+O(h^2)`. The target-time intervention has RHS `4h^2*k` and error `(1/2)*h^2*(1-3^(-k))`. All saved numerical states match their respective recurrence within 5.40e-11, including startup.

[Report and reproduction instructions](https://github.com/Unjuno/concentration-aware-ns/blob/a3269f2/reports/su2-bdf2-source-time.md) include the six raw archives, image identities, protocol and a replay checker that reads restart fields and residual histories. This is not a fresh master-binary test or validation of a general fix. I agree that stored-state/target-time semantics should be separated and boundary, restart and other consumers reviewed before changing `PhysicalTime` globally. The BDF2 control now provides a concrete regression case for that review.
